title: Rice pudding with cinnamon
description: Creamy rice slowly cooked in milk with vanilla and lemon peel, dusted with cinnamon.

steps.text: Put the rice and {300 ml} water in a heavy-based pot and bring to the boil. Simmer on low heat for 8 minutes until the water is almost all absorbed.
steps.tip: Short-grain rice (sold as rice for rižoto) gives the creamiest pudding.

steps: Meanwhile peel a long strip of lemon peel with a vegetable peeler, leaving the white part behind.
Pour in the milk, add the sugar, vanilla sugar and lemon peel and bring slowly to a gentle simmer.

steps.text: Cook on the lowest heat for 30 minutes, stirring every few minutes and scraping the bottom, until the rice is very soft and the pudding is creamy.
steps.tip: Stop while it still looks a little runny: it thickens a lot as it cools. If it catches on the bottom, do not scrape the burnt bits in.

steps.text: Take out the lemon peel. Serve warm, or pour into bowls or a box and chill. Dust with cinnamon just before eating.
steps.tip: Keeps 3 days in the fridge, covered. Stir in a splash of milk if it is too thick the next day.

title: Apple and walnut crumble
description: Soft cinnamon apples under a crunchy oat, walnut and butter crumble. Lovely with yogurt.
steps: Heat the oven to 190 °C. Slice the apples into a dish with 20 g sugar and the cinnamon.
Rub the flour, oats, butter and remaining sugar together, then stir in the chopped walnuts.
Scatter over the apples and bake 35 minutes until golden. Serve with yogurt.

title: Dark chocolate mousse
description: Airy, rich mousse made with dark chocolate, eggs and a little whipped cream.
steps: Melt the chocolate over hot water and cool a little. Stir in the egg yolks.
Whip the cream softly. Whisk the whites with the sugar to soft peaks.
Fold the cream, then the whites, into the chocolate. Spoon into glasses and chill at least 3 hours.

title: Panna cotta with berry sauce
description: Silky vanilla cream set with a little gelatine, with a quick sauce of warm berries.
steps: Soak the gelatine in cold water for 5 minutes.
Heat the cream, milk and sugars until steaming, take off the heat and stir in the squeezed gelatine.
Pour into 6 glasses and chill for 4 hours.
Simmer the berries with the honey for 5 minutes, cool and spoon over.

title: Baked apples with walnuts and honey
description: Whole apples stuffed with walnuts, raisins and cinnamon and baked until soft. Simple autumn dessert.
steps: Heat the oven to 180 °C. Core the apples, leaving the bottoms whole.
Mix the chopped walnuts, raisins, honey and cinnamon and fill the apples. Top each with a little butter.
Bake 30 to 35 minutes until soft.

title: Palačinke with jam and walnuts
description: Thin Croatian crepes rolled with jam or ground walnuts and sugar.
steps: Whisk the flour, eggs, milk, salt and 1 tbsp oil into a smooth thin batter and rest 10 minutes.
Wipe a hot pan with a little oil and fry thin crepes, about 1 minute a side.
Spread with jam or sprinkle with ground walnuts and sugar, and roll up.

title: Rožata (Dubrovnik caramel custard)
description: Baked custard with a thin caramel layer, flavoured with lemon zest. Dubrovnik's favourite dessert.
steps: Heat the oven to 160 °C. Get a baking dish of about 20 cm (or small heatproof moulds) ready, and boil a kettle of water.

steps.text: Put the {100 g} sugar for the caramel in a small dry pan on medium heat. When it starts to melt at the edges, swirl the pan (do not stir) until it has all melted and turned amber, about 5 minutes.
steps.tip: Watch closely: it goes from golden to burnt in seconds. Take it off when it is the colour of honey. Hot caramel burns badly, so do not touch or taste it.

steps: Pour the caramel straight into the dish or moulds and tilt to coat the bottom. It sets hard, which is right.
Grate the lemon zest. Warm the milk with the zest in a pot until hot but not boiling, about 4 minutes.

steps.text: Whisk the eggs with the rest of the sugar and the vanilla sugar until just smooth. Pour in the hot milk slowly while whisking.
steps.tip: Whisk gently: lots of foam makes holes in the custard. Pour it through a sieve if you want it perfectly smooth.

steps.text: Pour the custard over the caramel. Stand the dish in a deep roasting tray and pour hot water from the kettle into the tray until it comes halfway up the dish.
steps.tip: The water bath keeps the heat gentle, so the custard sets silky instead of bubbly.

steps.text: Bake for 45 to 50 minutes, until set at the edges with a slight wobble in the middle.
steps.tip: A knife pushed in near the middle should come out clean. Small moulds need only about 30 minutes.

steps.text: Let it cool, then put it in the fridge overnight. To serve, run a knife around the edge, put a plate on top and turn it over quickly. The caramel runs down as a sauce.
steps.tip: Keeps 3 days in the fridge, covered.

title: Fritule (little Christmas doughnuts)
description: Small fried dough balls with raisins, lemon and a splash of rum flavour, rolled in icing sugar.

ingredients.note: for frying, some stays in the pan

steps.text: Warm the milk until it feels just warm on your finger, not hot. Grate the lemon zest.
steps.tip: Hot milk kills the yeast. Lukewarm, like a baby's bottle, is right.

steps.text: In a large bowl mix the flour, yeast and sugar. Add the eggs, yogurt, warm milk, lemon zest and raisins and beat with a wooden spoon for a few minutes into a smooth, soft, sticky batter.
steps.tip: It should be thicker than pancake batter and fall slowly from the spoon. Add a spoon of flour or milk to get there.

steps: Cover the bowl with a towel and leave it somewhere warm for 1 hour, until bubbly and almost doubled.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a small, deep pan on medium heat. Test it with a drop of batter: it should sizzle and rise straight away.
steps.tip: If the fritule brown in seconds and stay raw inside, the oil is too hot, so turn it down. Never leave hot oil alone on the stove.

steps.text: Dip a teaspoon in the oil, scoop a small spoonful of batter and push it into the oil with a second spoon. Fry 6 to 8 at a time for 3 minutes, turning, until golden all over.
steps.tip: Dipping the spoon in oil first lets the batter slide off easily.

steps.text: Lift them out with a slotted spoon onto kitchen paper. While they are still warm, roll them in the powdered sugar.
steps.tip: Best on the day. Keep leftovers in a closed tin and warm them briefly in the oven.

title: Tiramisu
description: Coffee-soaked biscuits layered with mascarpone cream and cocoa. Make it a day ahead.
steps: Make 300 ml strong coffee and let it cool.
Whisk the yolks with the sugar until pale, then beat in the mascarpone. Whisk the whites stiff and fold in.
Dip the biscuits quickly in the coffee and layer with the cream in a dish, twice.
Dust with cocoa and chill at least 6 hours.

title: Fudgy brownies
description: Dense chocolate brownies with a crackly top and walnuts. Cut into 16 small squares.
steps: Heat the oven to 180 °C and line a 20 x 30 cm tin.
Melt the chocolate and butter together. Whisk in the sugar, then the eggs one by one.
Fold in the flour, cocoa and chopped walnuts, pour into the tin and bake 22 to 25 minutes. It should still be soft in the middle. Cool before cutting.

title: Mandarin yogurt cake
description: Light, moist cake made with yogurt and oil and lots of mandarin zest and juice. Perfect in winter.
steps: Heat the oven to 180 °C and line a cake tin of about 24 cm with baking paper. Grate the zest of half the mandarins, then squeeze the juice of all of them.
Whisk the eggs and sugar for 3 to 4 minutes until pale and fluffy.
Whisk in the yogurt, oil, zest and half the juice.

steps.text: Mix the baking powder into the flour, then fold it into the batter with a spatula until there are no dry streaks.
steps.tip: Stop as soon as it is mixed. Too much stirring makes the cake tough.

steps.text: Pour into the tin and bake for 35 to 40 minutes, until golden and a skewer in the middle comes out clean.
steps.tip: Do not open the oven in the first half of the baking time, or the cake may sink.

steps.text: While the cake is still warm, poke it all over with a skewer and spoon the rest of the juice over it. Let it cool in the tin, then dust with the powdered sugar.
steps.tip: Keeps 4 days in a closed box.

title: No-bake cheesecake
description: Biscuit base with a creamy cottage cheese and cream cheese filling and berry topping. Sets in the fridge.
steps: Crush the biscuits, mix with the melted butter and press into a 22 cm tin. Chill.
Blend the cottage cheese smooth, then beat with the cream cheese, sugar and lemon juice.
Whip the cream and fold it in. Spread over the base and chill at least 6 hours.
Top with thawed berries before serving.

title: Homemade chocolate pudding
description: Smooth chocolate pudding cooked from milk, cocoa and cornflour, topped with a little cream.
steps: Whisk the cocoa, cornflour, sugars and 150 ml of the milk until smooth.
Bring the rest of the milk to the boil, whisk in the mixture and stir 2 minutes until thick.
Stir in the chopped chocolate and pour into bowls. Serve warm or chilled.

title: Winter fruit salad with honey yogurt
description: Mandarins, apple, pear, kiwi and pomegranate with honey yogurt and toasted almonds.
steps: Peel and slice the fruit into a bowl.
Mix the yogurt and honey.
Serve the fruit with the yogurt and chopped almonds.

title: Frozen yogurt bark
description: Thick yogurt spread on a tray with berries, chocolate and nuts, frozen and broken into pieces.
steps: Mix the yogurt and honey and spread 1 cm thick on a lined tray.
Scatter with berries, chopped chocolate and almonds.
Freeze 3 hours, then break into pieces. Keep in the freezer.

title: Carrot cake with cream cheese frosting
description: Moist spiced carrot cake with walnuts and raisins, topped with a light cream cheese frosting.
steps: Heat the oven to 175 °C. Whisk the eggs, sugar and oil.
Fold in the flour, baking powder, cinnamon, grated carrot, walnuts and raisins.
Bake in a lined tin for 40 to 45 minutes and cool completely.
Beat the cream cheese with the icing sugar and spread on top.

title: Berry clafoutis
description: A soft baked custard-pancake studded with berries. Five minutes to mix, then into the oven.
steps: Heat the oven to 190 °C and butter a baking dish. Scatter in the berries.
Whisk the eggs, sugar, flour and milk into a smooth batter and pour over.
Bake 30 to 35 minutes until puffed and set. Dust with icing sugar and serve warm.

title: Banana and cocoa nice cream
description: Frozen bananas blended into a creamy, ice-cream-like dessert with cocoa and peanut butter.
steps: Slice the bananas and freeze for at least 4 hours.
Blend with the cocoa, peanut butter and oat drink until smooth, scraping down the sides.
Eat straight away or freeze 30 minutes for a firmer scoop.

title: Walnut roll (orehnjača)
description: Soft yeast dough rolled around a sweet walnut filling. A holiday classic in every Croatian home.
steps: Dissolve the yeast in 200 ml warm milk with 1 tsp sugar. Knead with the flour, 60 g sugar, melted butter, 1 egg, salt and zest into a soft dough. Rise 1 hour.
Warm the rest of the milk with the rest of the sugar and vanilla sugar and pour over the ground walnuts. Cool.
Roll the dough out to a large rectangle, spread with the filling and roll up tightly. Rise 30 minutes on a lined tray.
Brush with the other egg and bake at 175 °C for 40 to 45 minutes. Cool before slicing.

title: Sour cherry strudel
description: Thin pastry sheets rolled around sour cherries, sugar and breadcrumbs, baked crisp and dusted with sugar.
steps: Heat the oven to 190 °C. Toast the breadcrumbs in 20 g butter until golden.
Lay out half the pastry sheets, brushing each with melted butter. Sprinkle with breadcrumbs, then the drained cherries, sugar and cinnamon.
Roll up, repeat with the rest, and bake 30 to 35 minutes until crisp.
Dust with icing sugar and serve warm.
